The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.

Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.

Rule prose and exact atomic checklist:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. Rule: LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

Preferred position:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.


Fallback position:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.


Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
1.5 “Fees” means the Implementation Fee.
1.6 “Implementation Fee” means the one-time implementation charge of USD 12,000 stated in the first Order Form.
21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
21.2 Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.
21.3 “Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-indemn-61c801db","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 20 INDEMNIFICATION","rationale":"Section 20 meets the preferred position. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, and Customer's violation of Applicable Law), with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications and combinations. Section 15.1 reinforces our data position by prohibiting sale, advertising use, cross-customer combination and model training without our written consent. No assignment of our IP or data to Vendor, no Vendor-owned deliverables without a licence back, and no joint ownership. Clause 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, and transfer by change of control to Customer's prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. Clause 24.3 applies a reasonable consent standard to other assignments, and clause 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees or reduce service on our change of control, with cooperation on successor administrative changes. Section 13 (p0056) is consistent, allowing transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor under a Section 24 assignment. Clause 12.3 expressly confirms Customer may engage any supplier and has made no exclusivity, non-compete or minimum-volume commitment, and clause 2.1 confirms there is no minimum quantity or purchase commitment and that declining further Order Forms is not a breach. Section 4 routes Affiliate demand through Order Forms only, with no requirement that Affiliate requirements be sourced from Vendor. Clause 12.2 (Vendor shall not market a competing analytics service) is exclusivity running in Customer's favour and is acceptable per the detection guidance. Remaining "exclusive" references (non-exclusive licence in 13.1, exclusive-remedy carve-outs, exclusive jurisdiction in 28.2) are unrelated to exclusive dealing. The subscription grant (13.1) expressly extends to Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf, with no notice precondition; paid-up software and embedded Vendor Technology (13.2) is licensed perpetually, irrevocably and royalty-free to Customer and its Affiliates with contractor support permitted; and 13.3 allows transfer to an Affiliate or successor under the Section 24 assignment right and limits revocation/suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a cure opportunity. Termination rights in Section 9 do not create any at-will revocation in Vendor's favour (9.1 requires uncured material breach; 9.4 is a Customer-side right). Clause 12.3 goes further and expressly confirms that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, or conducting business in any field or territory, and that no exclusivity, non-compete, MFC, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment has been made. The only competition restriction (12.4) binds Vendor and benefits us, so it is not flagged. The sole Customer-side prohibition elsewhere (13.4, reverse engineering of hosted source code, subject to the statutory carve-out) is a standard IP protection, not a field-of-use or non-compete restriction. Section 9.4 gives Customer an unconditional right to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form without cause; Section 29.4 fixes that notice period at thirty days, matching our preferred 30-day standard. Customer owes only accrued Fees (no early-termination fee or penalty), and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, reinforced by Section 10.2 (refund of prepaid recurring Fees). This is important given the three-year term in Section 8.1.

Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right at all: searches for "convenience", "without cause" and "Vendor may terminate" return no Vendor-side right, and Sections 9.1-9.3 limit Vendor to material breach and insolvency. Section 24.4 also bars Vendor from terminating on Customer's change of control, and Section 20.5 bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services. Nothing in §§ 4, 7 or 30, or elsewhere in the document (searches for "favourable", MFN, match-rights and third-party-terms language returned no other hits), obliges Northwind to extend Brightline best terms given to any third party or to match third-party offers. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Northwind / Brightline)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (for Customer)  
**Subject:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement  
**Findings reviewed:** 18 rules — 16 compliant, 2 deviations, 0 missing

---

## Executive summary

This draft is, on the whole, unusually favourable to us. The high-value protections all sit at or above our preferred position: Vendor's IP and data indemnity is uncapped by virtue of the Excluded Claims carve-out (§ 20, § 21.3); we own Deliverables and retain all Customer Data with a perpetual, royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor Technology (§§ 13–15); we hold an unconditional 30-day termination-for-convenience right with a prepaid-fee refund and no early-termination fee (§ 9.4, § 29.4, § 10.2); assignment, licence scope, warranties, insurance, audit, renewal and transition assistance all meet the playbook. There is no exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-commitment, non-solicit or Customer-side MFN obligation anywhere in the document, and § 12.3 affirmatively confirms as much. Governing law and venue are New York, as preferred, with no arbitration clause.

Two deviations remain, and both trace back to the same drafting defect. "Fees" is defined at §§ 1.5/1.6 as only the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, even though the term is used throughout to mean recurring and Order Form fees (§§ 7.1, 8.3, 10.2). The consequence is that the mutual liability cap in § 21.1 — already narrowed to amounts under "the first Order Form" — collapses to roughly USD 12,000 regardless of actual spend, which fails even our fallback. Separately, § 7.7 imposes liquidated damages on us of 15% of annual Fees per week of late payment, uncapped and triggered by a minor breach; that is walk-away territory under the playbook. We should treat the defective "Fees" definition as a document-wide fix, since read literally it would also narrow our § 9.4 refund right.

**Verification note:** the proposed redline to § 21.1 did not pass automated verification and requires manual drafting before it goes back to Vendor. The § 7.7 redline was repaired and verified.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |
| Low | **LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer** | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) |
| Low | **LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs** | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability (§ 21.1) |

### Deviation detail

**§ 7.7 — Liquidated damages payable by Customer (LD).** Liquidated damages of 15% of annual Fees per week of delay, triggered by late payment of any invoice and uncapped, can quickly exceed remaining contract value. Our preferred position is no Customer-payable liquidated damages; the fallback is a single early-termination amount capped at three months' fees. Because § 9.4 carries no early-termination fee, no capped LD amount is needed elsewhere. *Proposal:* convert § 7.7 so that no liquidated damages or penalty is payable by Customer for late payment, replaced by ordinary late-payment interest on undisputed amounts. Service credits running in our favour are unaffected. Verified (repaired).

**§ 21.1 — Cap basis (LOL-CAP).** Mutuality and the § 21.3 Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) plus the payment-obligation carve-back all meet the preferred position. The cap *basis* does not: with "Fees" defined as the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee and the cap further limited to the first Order Form, the ceiling is illusory and falls below even a six-month fee fallback. *Proposal:* re-base the mutual cap on amounts paid or payable under the Agreement in the 12 months preceding the claim, with a USD 1,000,000 floor, and confirm Customer's payment obligations are not damages — leaving mutuality, exclusions and Excluded Claims untouched. **Verification failed; redline to be drafted manually before issue.**

---

## Walk-away items

1. **§ 7.7 liquidated damages.** An uncapped 15%-of-annual-Fees-per-week penalty triggered by a minor payment breach is walk-away territory under the playbook. Removal of the penalty mechanic (interest only on undisputed late amounts) is a condition of signature.
2. **§ 21.1 cap basis.** A liability ceiling of approximately USD 12,000 irrespective of actual spend is effectively illusory and fails our fallback. A 12-month paid-or-payable basis with a meaningful floor is required; we should not proceed on the current basis.

---

## Next steps

1. **Manually draft the § 21.1 redline** and re-verify before the markup goes out, given the failed verification on the automated proposal.
2. **Issue the § 7.7 redline** removing Customer-payable liquidated damages in favour of interest on undisputed late amounts.
3. **Raise the "Fees" definition as a document-wide fix.** Sections 1.5/1.6 define "Fees" as the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee only, which is inconsistent with §§ 7.1, 8.3, 10.2 and 21.1, and read literally would narrow our § 9.4 refund. Align the definition with recurring and Order Form fees; this is the cleanest single amendment and resolves the root cause of both deviations.
4. **Confirm no further redlines.** The remaining 16 rules are compliant and should not be reopened; the Vendor-granted MFN (§ 7.6), the Vendor-side competing-service restriction (§ 12.4) and the § 24.4 change-of-control protections run in our favour and should be preserved as drafted.
5. **Note for the business (no action in the markup):** the § 9.4 convenience-termination notice period sits in § 29.4 rather than in § 9.4 itself — substantively correct but worth flagging to the contract owner for operational clarity.
"}
